newsitem.title: UK: Hk stocks in London quiet but HSBC leaps.
newsitem.headline: Hk stocks in London quiet but HSBC leaps.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks trading in London remained lifeless on Friday with only HSBC Holdings breaking the mould, rising on the back of a strong performance by its sterling shares, dealers said.
A "buy" recommendation on HSBC from Dresdner Kleinwort Benson booted the banking group's shares. Kleinwort valued the stock at 19.00 stg, helping push HSBC's sterling shares to a record 16.32 stg.
Its Hong Kong dollar shares firmed $3-1/2 from their Hong Kong close.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was up 32.14 points at 13,369.49 by 1423 GMT, with most of this rise accounted for by the gain in HSBC, dealers said.
After a brief mark-down on the back of stronger-than-expected U.S. February payrolls, the index recovered again in line with T-bonds and the FTSE, they said.
"The market came off and then rallied but there's very little business going on in any stock apart from HSBC," one trader said. "Most stocks are just trading around their Hong Kong close".
